questions.question: In a nonzero row, which entry is called the pivot?
options: The entry closest to the right edge.
The first entry of the row, even if it is zero.
The first nonzero entry of that row.
The largest entry of that row.

questions.question: Does a zero row have a pivot?
options: No, because it has no nonzero entry.
Yes, its pivot is always $0$.
Only if the matrix is square.
Yes, its pivot is in the first column.

questions.question: In row echelon form, how do pivot positions change as one moves down the rows?
options: Each pivot lies in exactly the same column as the pivot above.
Each pivot lies to the right of the pivot in the row above.
Each pivot lies to the left of the pivot above.
Pivot positions may move in any direction.

questions.question: What extra role does a pivot have in reduced row echelon form?
options: It must appear in the last column.
It is a leading $1$ and the only nonzero entry in its column.
It is the largest number in the whole matrix.
It must be negative if the row has negative entries.

questions.question: What do pivots indicate when solving a linear system?
options: They mark leading variables and the structure of the echelon form.
They mark variables that are automatically free.
They mark rows that should be deleted.
They mark entries that never change under row operations.

questions.question: What is the pivot of the row $(0,0,5,2)$?
options: The row has no pivot

questions.question: What is the pivot of the row $(1,3,0)$?
options: The row has no pivot

questions.question: What is the pivot of the row $(0,0,0)$?
options: $0$ in the last column.
$0$ in the first column.
Every entry is a pivot.
There is no pivot.

questions.question: In $\begin{pmatrix}0&2&1\\0&0&-3\end{pmatrix}$, where are the pivots?
options: At positions $(1,1)$ and $(2,2)$.
At positions $(1,2)$ and $(2,3)$.
At positions $(1,3)$ and $(2,3)$.
Only at position $(1,2)$.

questions.question: Which row has pivot $-2$?
Must a pivot be equal to $1$ before the matrix is reduced?
options: No, pivots must always be zero.
No, pivots can be any nonzero number outside reduced row echelon form.
Yes, every pivot in every echelon form must be $1$, in every case without exception.
Only pivots in square matrices may differ from $1$.

questions.question: What is the difference between a pivot and a pivot column?
options: A pivot is an entry; a pivot column is a column containing such an entry.
They are two names for the entire matrix.
A pivot is a column; a pivot column is a row.
A pivot is always a variable, while a pivot column is always a solution.

questions.question: Why are pivot columns important when identifying free variables?
options: Variables in pivot columns are always free.
Free variables are determined by the right-hand side only.
Variables in non-pivot columns are the candidates for free variables.
Every column after the first is automatically free.

questions.question: Which matrix has pivot columns $1$ and $3$?
options: $\begin{pmatrix}1&0&0\\0&2&3\end{pmatrix}$
$\begin{pmatrix}0&0&1\\0&0&0\end{pmatrix}$
$\begin{pmatrix}0&1&2\\0&0&4\end{pmatrix}$
$\begin{pmatrix}1&2&0\\0&0&4\end{pmatrix}$

questions.question: Which matrix violates the echelon requirement on pivot positions?
options: $\begin{pmatrix}1&0&0\\0&1&0\end{pmatrix}$
$\begin{pmatrix}1&2&3\\0&0&1\end{pmatrix}$
$\begin{pmatrix}0&1&0\\1&0&0\end{pmatrix}$
$\begin{pmatrix}0&1&0\\0&0&1\end{pmatrix}$

questions.question: For the RREF $\begin{pmatrix}1&0&2&0\\0&1&-1&0\end{pmatrix}$, which variables are leading variables?
options: Only $x_4$

questions.question: Why does multiplying a nonzero row by $-3$ not change the pivot position?
options: Negative pivots are not allowed.
The row becomes a zero row.
The first nonzero entry stays in the same column.
The pivot must move to the last nonzero entry.

questions.question: Can a negative number be a pivot?
options: Only in reduced row echelon form.
No, pivots must be positive.
Yes, a pivot only needs to be the first nonzero entry of its row.
Only if the matrix has no positive entries, regardless of the specific input chosen.

questions.question: How many pivots does $\begin{pmatrix}1&0&2\\0&0&3\\0&0&0\end{pmatrix}$ have?
Which row operation can change the pivot value from $5$ to $1$ without changing its pivot column?
options: Add a new column to the matrix.
Swap the row with a zero row.
Multiply the row by $\frac{1}{5}$.
Delete all entries to the right of the pivot.
